newsitem.title: CANADA: Nine hour frost in central Alberta, clouds, rain.
newsitem.headline: Nine hour frost in central Alberta, clouds, rain.

text.p: Frost struck south and central Alberta and southwest Saskatchewan Thursday morning, Environment Canada said.
Edmonton, Alberta, saw 0 Celsius (32 F) for nine hours at chest level, meteorologist Mike Russo said.
Ground temperatures can be 2.0 to 5.0 Celsius cooler.
About 50 percent of central Alberta's crops were combined by Monday, Alberta Agriculture said.
Calgary saw -3.0 Celsius with temperatures below freezing for seven hours, Russo said.
Southern Alberta's harvest was 80 to 90 percent complete by Monday, Alberta Agriculture said.
Cypress Hills, in southwest Saskatchewan, saw -1.0 Celsius for four hours, and Val Marie 0 for three hours.
The region's harvest was delayed in the past week as more than one inch of rain fell there. Harvest was 85 percent done around Val Marie, Saskatchewan Agriculture said Monday.

Alberta should see showers with highs of eight to 13 Celsius. Saskatchewan should see clouds in the south and highs near 10 Celsius. Manitoba should see scattered rain with highs of eight to 14 Celsius.
